class ara::core::StringView

[SWS_CORE_02001]

class StringView {...};

Implementation of std::basic_string_view type from [string.view]

Header file#include "ara/core/string_view.h"

Scopenamespace ara::core

User Guide AI generated

Automatically generated description, content derived from the referenced AUTOSAR R25-11 documents (SWS specification and accompanying standard documents) — not an official AUTOSAR text. Statements marked as interpretation are conclusions drawn from the sources.

intended use

ara::core::StringView implements std::basic_string_view with value, pointer and reference types [SWS_CORE_02001] [SWS_CORE_02100] [SWS_CORE_02101] [SWS_CORE_02103] specialized for char. It can be used independently of ara::core::Initialize and Deinitialize [SWS_CORE_15002].

Generation & destruction

The view can be created empty, from const char* with or without length or via copy/move. Construction, copy/move assignment and destruction are constexpr, noexcept and exception-safe [SWS_CORE_02112] [SWS_CORE_02113] [SWS_CORE_02114] [SWS_CORE_02115] [SWS_CORE_02117] [SWS_CORE_02116] [SWS_CORE_02118] [SWS_CORE_02119].

Lifecycle & Ownership

The class is a view and provides a const pointer via data() [SWS_CORE_02136]. The interface does not describe a transfer of ownership of the underlying characters; The lifetime of the referenced memory must therefore match the usage of the view.

Interaction with other classes

In addition to iterators and size queries, the type offers prefix/suffix removal, comparisons, contains, search functions, as well as substr() [SWS_CORE_02120] [SWS_CORE_02128] [SWS_CORE_02137] [SWS_CORE_02138] [SWS_CORE_02142] [SWS_CORE_02154] [SWS_CORE_02157] [SWS_CORE_02141]. BasicString accepts and creates this view in several interfaces [SWS_CORE_03302] [SWS_CORE_03308] [SWS_CORE_03301].

Limitations & Error handling

at(), position-based comparisons, copy() and substr() trigger a IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation instead of std::out_of_range from [SWS_CORE_02133] [SWS_CORE_02143] if the position is invalid [SWS_CORE_02140] [SWS_CORE_02141]. The specified StringView operations are exception-safe [SWS_CORE_02131] [SWS_CORE_02156] [SWS_CORE_02158].

UTF-8 view and lifetime limit

The core specification maps StringView to string views and limits them to char in the Adaptive Platform because the platform uses UTF-8 throughout. The key is the lifespan rule: the programmer ensures that the view does not outlive its character storage array. SWS Core §7.4 “Core data types” SWS Core §7.4.2 “Data types derived from the C++ standard”

The language binding distinguishes modeled string data types and their C++ aliases. Interpretation: StringView is a suitable reading API view if a generated string should not require a transfer of ownership; however, the model binding itself defines the specific string type generated. SWS LanguageBinding §7.1 “C++ binding for CppImplementationDataTypes” SWS LanguageBinding §8.2.2 “String Data Type”

                      function at [SWS_CORE_02133]
                      

                      constexpr const_reference at (size_type pos) const noexcept;
                      

                      As per corresponding usage in [string.view] except for the following deviations: 1. The function is noexcept 2. if (pos >= size()) IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised instead of std:: out_of_range
                      

                      Technical classification AI generated
                      Automatically supplemented technical classification of the documentation assistant - no normative AUTOSAR text.
                      The behavior of this element is not formulated independently in the specification, but is defined by reference to the ISO C++ standard section [string.view]; The relevant counterpart is std::basic_string_view::at (cppreference: std::basic_string_view). Deviations from the std semantics according to the specification: the function is declared noexcept and therefore does not report errors via exceptions; instead of std::out_of_range, the violation IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is triggered (condition according to the specification: “if (pos >= size())”). Unlike the catchable std exception, a violation is not treatable: it is considered a violated pre/post condition ([SWS_CORE_00021]) and leads to abnormal process termination via Abort() ([SWS_CORE_00090]). The record is marked in the SWS Core as DRAFT, the content is therefore not yet binding.

                                                              function compare [SWS_CORE_02147]
                                                              

                                                              constexpr int compare (size_type pos1, size_type n1, const char *s, size_type n2) const noexcept;
                                                              

                                                              As per corresponding usage in [string.view] except for the following deviations: 1. The function is noexcept 2. if (pos1 > size()) IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised instead of std:: out_of_range
                                                              

                                                              Technical classification AI generated
                                                              Automatically supplemented technical classification of the documentation assistant - no normative AUTOSAR text.
                                                              The behavior of this element is not formulated independently in the specification, but is defined by reference to the ISO C++ standard section [string.view]; The relevant counterpart is std::basic_string_view::compare (cppreference: std::basic_string_view). Deviations from the std semantics according to the specification: the function is declared noexcept and therefore does not report errors via exceptions; instead of std::out_of_range, the violation IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is triggered (condition according to the specification: “if (pos1 > size())”). Unlike the catchable std exception, a violation is not treatable: it is considered a violated pre/post condition ([SWS_CORE_00021]) and leads to abnormal process termination via Abort() ([SWS_CORE_00090]). The record is marked in the SWS Core as DRAFT, the content is therefore not yet binding.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          function substr [SWS_CORE_02141]
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          constexpr StringView substr (size_type pos=0, size_type n=npos) const noexcept;
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          As per corresponding usage in [string.view] except for the following deviations: 1. if (pos > size()) IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised instead of std:: out_of_range
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Technical classification AI generated
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Automatically supplemented technical classification of the documentation assistant - no normative AUTOSAR text.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The behavior of this element is not specified independently in the specification, but is defined through the reference to ISO C++ standard section [string.view]; the corresponding counterpart is std::basic_string_view::substr (cppreference: std::basic_string_view). Deviations from std semantics according to the specification: instead of std::out_of_range, violation IsoStdOutOfRangeViolation is raised (condition according to the specification: “if (pos > size())”). Unlike the catchable std exception, a violation cannot be handled: it is considered a violated precondition/postcondition ([SWS_CORE_00021]) and leads to abnormal process termination through Abort() ([SWS_CORE_00090]). The record is marked DRAFT in SWS Core; its content is therefore not yet binding.
